subject: Errde
fact: Errde is the guardian of the city against corruption, linked to the Council of Savants and possibly the Clan Lairds, and holds the key to uncovering the conspiracy centered on Droki. She can guarantee freedom and safe passage in exchange for Droki and proof of corruption.
source_quote: It is my job to protect the city from corruption. So yes, it is for the city.

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is the central figure in the corruption at the Deepking’s court, linked to the Council of Savants and possibly elements of the Clan Lairds. His discovery is essential to proving the conspiracy.
source_quote: Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognizes corruption through the lens of the Blade Bazaar, having witnessed and replicated its behaviors — grift, chaos, and rule-breaking — and identifies systemic corruption in authoritarian structures.
source_quote: Yes, there was much of that going on.

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants is implicated in the corruption at the Deepking’s court, with Droki linked to its activities and possibly complicit in undermining its rules.
source_quote: He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: Clan Lairds
fact: The Clan Lairds are suspected of involvement in the corruption at the Deepking’s court, with Droki possibly tied to their clandestine operations.
source_quote: He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: escaped slaves
fact: A group of Drow may be searching for escaped slaves; Errde can deny their presence in the city, and her ability to provide this cover is a leverage point for Thorin’s freedom.
source_quote: If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here.

subject: corruption escalation
fact: Corruption began with rule-breaking in the bazaar, escalated to grift, then chaos, and now threatens destruction, as described by Errde and confirmed by Daz’s observations.
source_quote: Things were not proceeding according to the rules of the market, of the bazaar. It starts with not obeying the rules. Then it proceeds to grift, then chaos, and then destruction.

subject: 175 gold pieces of equipment
fact: Errde offers 175 gold pieces of equipment from the armory as a reward for initial cooperation, with another 175 gold pieces contingent on delivering Droki and proof of corruption.
source_quote: As a reward, I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.

subject: the city
fact: The city is the primary domain of the corruption, with the Deepking’s court at its heart, and Errde asserts her role as its protector against internal decay.
source_quote: There is something very wrong going on in my city. Some kind of corruption eats at the heart of the Deepking’s court.

subject: proof of corruption
fact: Errde claims Daz’s description of the Blade Bazaar’s behaviors constitutes proof of corruption, linking systemic lawlessness in commerce to political decay.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is seeking clarity on whether to align with the Stone Guards or the City, and is being manipulated by Errde’s promises of freedom and rewards in exchange for action against Droki.
source_quote: Look, we want to know if this is for the Stone Guards or the City?
